PullRequest.Title: Copilot setup: let the keyboard reach the Learn more link
PullRequest.Body:

Part of microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#7531. Fixes microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9998 (from test plan item microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9852).

The **Learn more** link on the Windows setup's **GitHub Copilot CLI** page wasn't a tab stop, so keyboard users couldn't reach it: Tab only cycled through the options and Back, Next and Cancel. It's now a tab stop, and Space opens it.

Known limitations, left as they are:
- Enter on the link moves to the next page, because the wizard's default **Next** button takes Enter.
- The link is Inno Setup's `TNewLinkLabel`. UI Automation exposes it as a pane named with the whole note, including the link markup, so screen readers may read the markup.

### How to test
1. Run the User Installer with Copilot CLI not installed, and go to the **GitHub Copilot CLI** page.
2. Press Tab from the selected option: focus moves to the link before Back, Next and Cancel.
3. Press Space: the Copilot CLI install docs open in the browser.

### Validation
- Stub user installer driven with UI Automation, before and after the change, with the link pointed at a local script that records the click:
  - before: Tab never reached the link (failed);
  - after: the first Tab reaches it (passed), and Space opens it (passed).
- ISCC compile of the user and system x64 installers with the Copilot shim: passed.
- Installer Pascal harness: 90 of 90 passed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Interactive Windows installer reaches and constructs the GitHub Copilot CLI choice page
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After leaving the task-selection page, the existing probe wait and CopilotPreparePage run; the basic or full page is built once behind CopilotBasicPageBuilt/CopilotFullPageBuilt. Setting Link.TabStop during that one-time construction is a constant-time property assignment and adds no boundary work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing Copilot probe is started and awaited before page preparation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one probe sequence per installer flow, independent of the footer link and unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same probe and wait occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing wait can gate page preparation, but Link.TabStop is assigned only afterward during local UI construction and does not add to or repeat the probe.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One footer link control on one selected Copilot page per installer run; page builders are guarded against reconstruction.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single installer UI thread; page construction is serialized and occurs at most once for each page kind.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The page-built booleans act as one-run construction caches. The diff does not alter cold construction, warm revisits, cache keys, invalidation, coalescing, or failure behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the complete one-hunk diff and traced guarded page builders.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No material uncertainty: the changed operation is a single Boolean assignment on one control.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression. The change adds only constant one-time local UI work and does not move existing probe work onto a new path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Keyboard navigation tabs to the Learn more link
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each Tab key advances focus through the wizard's existing tab order. The changed TabStop property makes the existing link eligible; no click callback, subprocess, filesystem, network, IPC, or serialization work runs merely on focus.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One additional focusable control in a small fixed wizard page; cost does not scale with repositories, files, history, or user data.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous single-threaded UI focus traversal; no spawned or queued work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is read or populated on focus; cold and repeated traversal have the same constant local cost.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: the diff only sets TabStop and the link's sole callback is OnLinkClick, not a focus event.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact control-library focus bookkeeping is not measured, but cardinality is fixed at one added tab stop and no expensive boundary is reachable from focus alone.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable synchronous-UI regression; one extra fixed tab stop has negligible bounded work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Keyboard activation opens the Copilot CLI Learn more documentation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Pressing Space while focused invokes the existing CopilotLinkClick handler, which calls ShellExecAsOriginalUser with ewNoWait. This user-requested launch is the scenario's intended operation and is not awaited on the installer critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Ask the OS shell to open the documentation URL in the user's browser.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One non-blocking shell invocation per explicit click or keyboard activation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The identical boundary was already reached by mouse activation; the diff only makes the existing control keyboard-focusable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the installer progress critical path because ewNoWait is used; it occurs only when the user explicitly requests Learn more.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One shell-open request per explicit activation, matching the pre-diff mouse-click path; no collection fan-out or automatic repetition.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each activation can issue one asynchronous shell-open operation; ordinary usage is one explicit action, with no diff-added loop, scheduler, or burst mechanism.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache is involved. Browser/OS URL handling cache state is external and unchanged; there is no changed positive, negative, or coalescing behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the existing OnLinkClick assignment and ShellExecAsOriginalUser call flow.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser startup cost varies by machine, but it is explicitly requested, non-blocking, and neither newly implemented nor amplified in cardinality by the diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable boundary-fanout or latency regression. The diff exposes an existing one-shot action to another input modality without adding work to normal installer progress.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete changed-file inventory and full diff for the performance focus. The sole change sets TabStop on one existing installer link. Traced one-time page construction, keyboard focus traversal, and explicit link activation through the existing shell boundary; no hot-path, scaling, retention, concurrency, cache-lifecycle, or critical-path regression was introduced.
